bundle.note: The enrollment bundle (identity-enrollment.md §5.4): an unsigned CBOR map carrying the device_cert and card above. Unsigned because both members are signed already; what has to be checked is that the card belongs to the identity the certificate names, which it does here.

fields.attestations: [the signed attestation above, embedded as a map]
fields.name: Alice

card_successor.note: A card that pre-commits a successor identity (§3.4). A server that has cached this card must refuse a later card for the same identity carrying a different successor, or none.

enroll_request.note: A renewal request (identity-enrollment.md §4, §8) that also carries a `pair` tag from the QR path (§5.6), so one vector exercises every field. `prev` is the device_cert above, and names the same device as this request; `pair` is HMAC-SHA-256(pairing_secret, device). Signed by the *device* key, not the identity key — the object names the only key that could have signed it.

enroll_session_claim.note: A holder proving to a mailbox that it holds the identity key whose renewals it is asking to stand by for (identity-enrollment.md §5.1). Signed by the *identity* key, unlike the enroll_request above. `session` is SHA-256 of `session_secret`, the secret the mailbox handed the holder when it opened the session, so a captured claim is worth nothing against any other session; the secret is published here only so the hash can be rechecked.

freeze.note: Signed by keys.registrar. `frozen` is CBOR true (0xf5).

login_proof_v2.note: The v = 2 proof: v = 1's fields and `host`, the authority the client addressed, in canonical form (hotline-ng-auth.md §6.2). Same domain; `v` tells the two apart. A server that received it with any other Host refuses it.

notes: All byte strings are lowercase hex.
Seeds are the 32-byte Ed25519 private key seeds (RFC 8032). Device X25519 secret = SHA-256("hl-identity/device-enc/v1" || seed).
signature_input_hex = domain || 0x00 || unsigned_hex; signature_hex = Ed25519(seed, signature_input).
signed_hex is the deterministic CBOR of the unsigned map plus a `sig` entry, keys sorted by encoded bytes.
Fingerprint = SHA-256(public key), shown as lowercase Crockford base32, 52 digits.
`rejects` entries must fail to parse with the named error; implementations that don't distinguish error kinds should at least fail.
`pair` = HMAC-SHA-256(key = pairing_secret, message = device public key), 32 bytes.
The bundle is the one object here with no signature of its own; `encoded_hex` rather than `signed_hex` says so.

Registrar objects (identity-registrar.md §4) sign like every other. The rotation has a second signature: ack_input_hex = domain || "/ack" || 0x00 || unsigned_hex, where unsigned_hex is the map without `sig` *and* `ack`; ack_hex is Ed25519(successor seed, ack_input).
A record list's `entries` are [seq, bytes] pairs; each bytes is a record with its own signature, verified on its own. Its `fingerprint` is SHA-256 of the key the list was asked for.

records.note: keys.identity's per-identity list, signed by keys.registrar. `fingerprint` is the one the list was asked for; `entries` are [seq, record bytes], each record the vector of the same name. Seq 3 is another identity's record and is not in this list.

records_empty.note: An empty per-identity list: the registrar holds nothing against keys.other. Signed, so a cache can hold it.

register.note: A first registration: an invite as `proof`, and a `successor` commitment to keys.successor.

register_reissue.note: A reissue: the same handle, no proof, the same commitment — dropping it would be refused.

rejects.name: duplicate map key, otherwise in canonical order
map keys out of canonical order
more attestations than a card may carry
device revocation signed by a device whose certificate lacks manage
rotation acknowledged by a key other than the successor
server challenge with a host not in canonical form

revoke_attestation.note: Signed by keys.registrar: every attestation of alice@hl.example to keys.identity issued at or before `time` is void.

revoke_device.note: Signed by the identity key. `device` is keys.lost_device.

revoke_device_by_device.note: Signed by keys.device, carrying its own certificate as `signer_cert`: unrestricted caps, so `manage`. The signature is by `signer`, not the identity.

rotate.note: `sig` by the predecessor (keys.identity) and `ack` by the successor (keys.successor), both over unsigned_hex — the map without `sig` and `ack` — under the domain and the domain with `/ack` appended.

server_challenge.note: The server's signature over the challenge it issued (hotline-ng-auth.md §6.2 step 1), by the server key above. A client that addressed hl.example:5700 and was given this challenge under this key accepts it until expires, plus its skew.

article_signed_parent.note: An article (§3.4) replying to article 41, itself signed by keys.other under id 33..33.

article_unsigned_parent.note: An article replying to article 40, which is unsigned: `parent` holds `article` alone.

canonical_text.name: CR LF and lone CR mixed

cert_window.note: Lobby lines like chat_lobby, each with a certificate of its own, read at `at` = `sent` (§3.5): valid at t when `expires` is after `issued`, `issued` <= t + S and t <= `expires` + S, S = 600.

chat_action.note: An action in the lobby: `act` true.

chat_lobby.note: A public line in the lobby (§3.3): room 0.

chat_room.note: A public line in room 70000, a four-byte room id. Its text crossed a link with CR line endings, as `texts` gives it, and verifies once canonicalized.

deniable_box.note: private_message's map without `sig`, which is its unsigned_hex, padded for a deniable box and sealed in auth mode under keys.device's X25519 key (§3.11). sealed_hex is 0x02, pkS, enc and the ciphertext.

message_cert.note: The certificate every signed message here carries: keys.device under keys.identity, caps 3 (login and message) and no name, which a certificate meant for messages leaves out (e2e-messages.md §2).

messages.note: Signed messages (e2e-messages.md §3). Each is read as its server received it at `at`; `cert` is message_cert unless a vector says otherwise. detached_hex is the whole map without its text keys (`text`, or `subject` and `body`), sig kept; link_hex is the detached form with `cert` replaced by `cert_sha256`, its SHA-256 (§5). Reassembling either, with the text and (for a link form) the certificate, gives back unsigned_hex once `sig` is removed. `texts` are as a reader was handed them, canonicalized before they are put back (§3.1). A read with its own `at` is read then, and `sent_apart` says `sent` is more than S from it. message_rejects name an `object` and a `form` (whole, detached or link; for a padded_plaintext, signed or deniable), with the `texts` and, for a link form, the fetched `cert_hex` a reader was handed, and must fail with `error`.

mixed_order_key.note: A device key A = keys.device's point plus a point of order 8: not of small order, so accepted when the cofactorless equation [S]B = R + [k]A holds (k = 0 mod 8 here), and rejected when only the cofactored one does (§3.1). Both are lobby lines under a certificate naming A.

private_message.note: A private message signed and not sealed (§3.2), to keys.other's identity.

sealed.note: Sealed messages (e2e-messages.md §3.7-§3.11), HPKE (RFC 9180) with DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256), HKDF-SHA256 and AES-256-GCM. Each is sealed to `recipient`, a device of keys.other's identity whose X25519 secret derives from its seed as keys.device's does, and from keys.device, whose public_enc_hex is the deniable box's pkS. A reader opens each at `now` by its own clock, received at `at`, its session having proved `recipient.identity_fingerprint`, with the sender shown as keys.identity, and with a replay memory that holds nothing. ikm_e_hex is the ikm RFC 9180's DeriveKeyPair makes the ephemeral key from, ephemeral_secret_hex and enc_hex the pair it makes; padded_hex is the plaintext as sealed, and sealed_hex the box. sealed_rejects name the state of §8 each opens in (`expect`) and the error it carries.

sealed_message.note: private_message's whole map, signature and all, padded and sealed (§3.8): the two share their signature.

sealed_rejects.name: a deniable box whose certificate's device_enc is not the pkS AuthDecap used
a deniable box with another pkS swapped in, which fails to open
the deniable box opened under base mode and the base info

rotate_successor.note: keys.successor rotating on to keys.successor_successor, as `rotate` takes keys.identity to keys.successor: `sig` by the first and `ack` by the second.

notes: Friendship objects (proposals/friendship-objects.md). `now` is the checker's clock and `skew` is S.

friend_objects are signed as the objects above are, each naming its `object` (offer, acceptance, withdrawal or device_cert) and its `signer` in `keys`. keys.identity, keys.successor and keys.successor_successor sign with keys.device, under message_cert, cert_successor and cert_successor_successor; keys.other with keys.other_device, under cert_other. A friendship is the array of its offer's and its acceptance's bytes, `array_hex`, named by `hash_hex`, its SHA-256. `rotate` takes keys.identity to keys.successor, and `rotate_successor` keys.successor on to keys.successor_successor.
friend_pairs: `pair_hex` = SHA-256(input_hex), input_hex = "hl-identity/friend-pair/v1" || 0x00 || the lesser fingerprint || the greater, however the two are ordered.

friend_rejects must be refused at `step`, checked at `now` with nothing held: an offer alone (§3: step 1 without the array, then 3 to 6), a friendship whole, and a withdrawal by the steps that need no pair (§4: 1, 2, 5 and 6). `error` names this implementation's error; the step binds.

friend_reads check `vector` at `now`, the case's own when it gives one, against the pair's two fingerprints `pair`, the rotation records applied (`rotations`, by name), and the withdrawals held (`withdrawals`, by name, each checked whole against `pair` with no rotation applied, as when it was taken). An offer or a friendship is checked by §3, a withdrawal by all six steps of §4; rotations enter only a withdrawal's step 4, never a withdrawal already held. `expect` is accepted or the step it fails at; `error` as above. A case may carry a `note`.
friend_cert_window: offers like `offer`, each under a certificate of its own, checked at `now`. A certificate is valid at t when `expires` is after `issued`, `issued` <= t + S and t <= `expires` + S.

offer.note: keys.identity offers keys.other a friendship, under message_cert.

withdrawal_by_offeree.note: keys.other spreading withdrawal_by_offerer, naming keys.identity as `party`: ends what it ends.

withdrawal_by_offerer.note: keys.identity on its own account, `party` absent: ends `friendship`, whose offer predates `before`, and leaves `friendship_again` standing.

withdrawal_offeree_own.note: keys.other on its own account: ends `friendship`, whose acceptance predates `before`, and leaves `friendship_reaccepted`, the same offer accepted again after it, standing.
